spec: Headline in a neo-grotesque or geometric sans, weight 450-600, 48-72px, line-height 1.0-1.1, tracking -0.02 to -0.03em, one near-black or near-white ink, two lines broken by hand at a phrase, 24-44 characters. Sub at 16-20px, one ink step down, 16-32px below.

Headline at 56-108px in a sans of weight 400-600 or a high-contrast serif, tracking -0.045 to -0.07em, line-height 0.95-1.1, under 50 characters. Stop while every letter pair still shows a sliver of ground; faces with a tight display cut stop near -0.045em. Relax as size falls: -0.06em at 64px, -0.04em at 48px, -0.015em at 32px.

Headline at weight 400 only, 48-116px, line-height 1.0-1.1, tracking -0.01 to -0.03em, black or warm near-black, flush left, one line if it fits. Allow no bold heading anywhere on the page. Hierarchy comes from size and ink alone; labels drop to 11-13px mono or small caps.

Headline in a weight 200-300 sans, at least 64px on light and 48px on dark, tracking -0.02 to -0.04em, line-height 0.85-1.1, one or two lines, on a plain ground. Keep controls at weight 500 so the thin type reads as a decision, not a font-loading fallback.

Headline in weight 700 sentence case, 48-80px, line-height 1.0, tracking -0.025 to -0.035em, near-black, a short plain sentence ending in a full stop. H2s keep the ratio at about 42/48 and -0.035em, two lines at most. Never leave tracking at default on bold.

One serif used only for H1 and H2, weight 300-500, 44-80px (up to 128px on dark manifesto pages), line-height 1.0-1.1, tracking 0 to -0.03em, single ink, never bold. All UI, labels and body stay sans or mono, so the serif alone carries the voice.

One serif family, 54-96px, weight 300-500, line-height 0.95-1.1, tracking -0.01 to -0.03em. Turn one word or the closing phrase into the true italic at the same size and weight, usually on line two. The italic must carry the meaning. Sub in full ink at weight 500, not pale grey.

Grotesque heading, weight 450-600, 48-88px, tracking -0.01 to -0.02em. One word or phrase swaps to an italic serif at weight 400 on the same line. Scale the swap to match x-heights, usually 1.02-1.1em, and reset its tracking to 0. One swap per heading, repeated through H2s.

One size, 32-64px, weight 400-600, line-height 1.0-1.25, tracking 0 to -0.03em. Two clauses split by tone: first at full ink, second at 45-60% ink, on a second line or running on. Alternatives: drop weight two steps, or change case. This block replaces the subhead.

Headline in one ink with a single clause or final line in one flat brand colour, no gradient, same size and weight, 46-80px, line-height 1.0-1.1. The coloured words are the claim, not decoration. Repeat the hue on the primary action, or take it from the hero photograph.

Clip a small tonal gradient to the headline: full ink at top-left to 60-70% ink at bottom-right, no hue shift, 52-96px, weight 400-500, on a dark or pale ground. It should read as light falling on letters. Keep the first words at full ink so the line stays crisp.

Flat ink headline, 60-128px, with only the closing phrase clipped to a two-stop gradient taken from the logo or a product colour, or with one dark stop near the ink so the shift is subtle. Never gradient the whole headline. Repeat on H2s only if it is the signature.

One word in a 44-90px headline gets one mark: an SVG hand stroke 3-6px thick under the baseline, a flat highlighter block, or a selection rectangle of radius 4-6px. Overrun the word by 4-10px, break at descenders, and vary the stroke between headings so it never looks stamped.

Uppercase headline in a condensed or neo-grotesque cut, 56-120px, line-height 0.8-0.95, tracking 0 to -0.04em, short lines of near-equal length so the text locks into one block. Pair with thin sentence-case body at 16-20px. Reserve it for headlines, never nav or labels.

Extended black cut, weight 700-900, uppercase or sentence case, 40-78px, line-height 0.8-1.05, tracking 0 to -0.01em, two to four short lines. Width supplies the presence, so size can stay modest. Set everything around it small and light, at 13-18px.

One display face with strong character (soft serif, chunky rounded, fat retro, custom) at weight 400-800, 48-90px, line-height 0.95-1.2, tracking 0 to -0.02em, in a deep brand colour instead of black, on a flat or pastel ground. Keep the sans beside it completely plain.

H1 at only 28-48px, weight 400-500, line-height 1.1-1.3, one or two lines, and nothing on the page is larger. On utility pages use one word at 48-64px with 90-120px of air above and below. Scale comes from images, tables or whitespace, never from the type.

The product or brand name alone is the headline, 56-80px, weight 500-600, tight tracking, centred, no verb. Beneath it a five or six word promise at 21-28px weight 400, roughly 2:1 with the name. A short status word can replace the promise. Let the object fill the frame.

Two short lines at 100-390px, line-height 0.75-1.05, tracking -0.02 to -0.04em, anchored to a corner or stepped across the viewport instead of centred, running past the fold or overlapped by images. No subhead beside it. Use once, on a page of quiet small type.

Each headline line rests on its own 1px rule in the pale line colour, either cut to that line's width for a stepped edge or full-bleed like ledger paper. 72-125px, weight 300-400, rule 8-14px under the baseline. Keep rules very quiet.

Fixed opening words with one slot at the end cycling 3-5 nouns, masked to the line height and moved vertically over 400-600ms, or typed with a cursor. Reserve the widest word's width, or centre so the whole line re-centres. Hold each word 2-3 seconds. Stop for reduced motion.

A full sentence or list takes the headline job, 35-80px, weight 400-500, line-height 1.1-1.2, with no size or weight change inside it, running 60-100% of the container. Break lines by hand. Allow at most one inline object or underlined link. No subhead follows.

One paragraph at 32-48px, weight 300-500, line-height 1.0-1.2, left aligned, 780-1150px wide. First sentence in full ink, the rest runs on in the same line at about 6:1 contrast. No eyebrow, no subhead. Repeat for nearly every section. Use text-wrap: pretty, never balance.

Two lines at 26-34px, weight 350-500, tight tracking: set-up in 50% ink, payoff in solid ink. Reverses the usual order so the eye lands on the last words. Any sub sits 6-8px below. Align the block's bottom edge to the neighbouring image, not its centre.

Left or centred stack repeated identically on every section: label at 12-20px, H2 at 36-52px weight 500-600, lede at 18-21px line-height 1.4-1.55 in the second ink, capped at 640-840px. Gaps 8-24px. Keep the three steps in one family, or two at most.

A short sentence with a full stop and no eyebrow, rule or subhead, 40-64px, weight 400-600, near-black, flush left or centred, 60-120px of air above and 24-64px below. Two short beats work well. It works only if the sentence states something specific.

Split the row: heading 40-88px on the left, a 16-22px note on the right, top or bottom aligned to the heading, starting just right of centre at about 55% of the container, 420-560px wide. A rail-to-rail rule about 60px below may close the row.

Two-line heading at 32-56px on the left; on the same bottom baseline at the far right one small control: a 32-48px button, text link, arrow pair or count. 40-64px down to content. Put the section action here rather than under the grid.

Each section opens with a 1px rule across the container, or 4px for editorial. Heading at 28-60px hangs 12-16px under it in the left third, broken by hand onto two tight lines; content starts on the same line in the next column. Never centre.

Heading sits in a ruled grid cell with a small index: a 16-30px number in muted ink or accent mono beside or above it, matching nav numbering if any. Title 30-80px weight 400, cell padding 24-40px. A folder-style slug can replace the number on developer pages.

Same size throughout, 30-56px: heading opens in sans 600 or serif roman, then turns to an italic serif at weight 400 for the feeling words. Optionally tint the italic one warm accent. Centred or left. Use on every section so it becomes the voice.

Heading in one ink, 36-64px, with one word, clause or line in an accent. The colour must mean something: product family, brand or section hue. On dark, one lit word can take a soft 20-24px glow of its own colour. One coloured element per heading.

One phrase in a 32-64px heading sits on a device: flat highlighter block, selection rectangle of radius 4-6px, bounding box with corner handles, inline code chip, or hand stroke. Choose the device the product itself uses. Same device on every section; the tint may change.

Every section opens with a loud block: 56-110px heavy or condensed caps, line-height 0.85-1.0, plus a quiet contrast voice directly above or below it, such as a 36px italic serif or 20px mono caps. Two tones of voice in one heading unit.

Modest heading in caps at 20-40px, tracking +0.04 to +0.1em, weight 400-600, in ink or a deep brand colour, left or centred. Reads as engraved, not shouted. Pair with a text link on the same baseline. Keep it under 30 characters.

A small line drawing about 85px tall centred above a serif heading at about 56px weight 500, 28px gap, 90px before content. Every major section opens the same way with a different drawing, so drawings act as chapter marks. Needs real illustration, not icons.

The heading is tied to scroll: pinned about 90px below the nav at 48px weight 300 while content moves beneath it, or rising into place over footage as a clip settles, at about 80/84 weight 700. One short phrase, legible at every scroll position.

Two heading voices with fixed jobs: serif at 40-48px for chapters, sans at 30-38px flush left for features inside them, or the reverse. The reader learns the level from the voice alone. Never mix the two voices on one level.

Five left-aligned lines in a centred block, each opening with the same short word in bold accent sans at about 54px, followed by a serif phrase at the same size, about 67px line step. Repetition turns a stance into the strongest type moment on the page.

Mono uppercase label, 11-14px, weight 400, tracking 0.05-0.12em, mid-grey at about 5.5:1 contrast, 12-24px above the heading and flush with it. One label style per page, also used for footer heads and data keys, so mono always means metadata.

A 6-10px brand-derived marker (dot, square, hexagon, tag shape), 8-12px gap, then 11-14px uppercase mono or sans, tracking 0.05-0.1em, mid-grey. The marker is nearly the only chroma on the page. Place it top-left of the section, 16-40px above the heading.

Wrap or prefix the label with syntax such as square brackets, a double colon, double underscores or a numbered slash. Mono 11-14px caps, the token at about 40% ink and the word at 90%. Use one pattern everywhere, including nav and FAQ.

Mono caps 11-13px in a rectangle 22-30px tall, radius 0-4px, 1px outline or pale tinted fill, 8-12px side padding, colour following the section. Reuse the same tag for rails, states and diagram nodes, not just section titles, so it reads as one system.

Sentence case, no tracking, weight 500, 13-18px in the section accent, 8-24px above the H2. The largest version matches body size and reads as the heading's first line. No caps, pill or icon. The accent can shift by section, and flips on dark bands.

Sans or serif caps at 11-16px, weight 400-500, tracking 0.08-0.2em and up to 0.3em at 11px, warm grey or brand tint, 10-16px above a serif or light heading. Use on section intros only, never on every block.

Uppercase 10-14px with no added tracking, or at most 0.04em, black or 60% ink, no box or marker. Sits flush to the grid or sticks to a panel's top-left at 10-14px inset. A 2px size step from body can be the entire hierarchy.

A tag 24-36px tall, radius 4-8px or full, sentence case 13-16px weight 500. Pale tint fill with text in the same hue at 8-12% strength, or a 1px outline. About 24px above the heading. Hue identifies a product or section, never decoration.

One news link above the H1, 32-40px tall, full or zero radius, 13-16px label with arrow or chevron, 24-50px above the headline. Use one distinct device: a dark pill on a pale hero, one bright fill, or a hairline border. It must link to a real item.
One badge beside a plan name: 10-12px weight 500-600, 20-22px tall, full radius. Grey on grey keeps the recommended plan calm; a 10% tint of the only accent marks it once. No second badge on the row.

A short line anchors the label: a 22-56px 1px rule before or above, a 1x12px tick, or a full-width hairline with the label 16px below. Label 12-15px in ink or accent. For editorial meta, stretch a rule between byline and read time at 11px caps.

Tiny labels pinned to the page, not the heading: 10-12px numerals in the gutter, paired edge labels on one baseline, or mono captions in viewport corners 24-36px in. They replace dividers and eyebrows. Keep at least 10px and one ink step readable.

Two lines under or over media: name at 15-18px weight 400-500, detail at 12-15px in uppercase grey or mono, 4-8px apart. Keep sizes between 12 and 18px site-wide so text behaves as caption. Category colour can follow the project accent.

A label treated as an object: a paper tab with a small index inset 24px on the hero frame, a sticker tilted 3-5 degrees over a headline edge, a filled colour cell, or a script note. One per screen. Works when the brand has a physical world to draw on.

One to two sentences under the H1: 16-20px, weight 400, line-height 1.4-1.5, 60-85% of the heading's ink strength, 16-32px below, capped near 30em or 500-640px. H1 to sub is about 3:1. Balance centred lines so no word is stranded.

A lead sentence at 22-28px, line-height 1.25-1.4, with one to four words lit. Lit by colour, italic or underline, the sentence stays in full ink; lit by ink, the base drops to muted. Size never changes. The lit words alone should summarise the offer.
Lead in the display face, not the text face, 24-26px weight 400-500, line-height 1.35-1.4, 55-60% ink, capped at 600px, directly under the heading. Same family means hierarchy comes only from grey.

Name and promise set as one block at the same 28-32px size with line-height near 1.05: name in ink, promise in mid-grey, no gap between them. Body at 16px follows 6-8px below. For tiles, plan names and product cards.

No H1 above it: the lead itself takes the first screen, 30-45px, line-height 1.0-1.25, regular weight, 620-900px wide, flush left or centred. Works when the sentence is unusually good, and when imagery or a wordmark supplies the scale.
One dry line at 20-48px placed in the clear area of a full-bleed photograph, 24px inset, with one 16px underlined link 24-30px below, black or white by image tone. No button, no scrim.

One clause or glyph run recoloured inside a 28-36px sub: a soft two-colour fill with no hard stops, or per-word product colours. First and last words stay plain. One per section, never in the headline too. Everything around it stays monochrome.

The sub demonstrates the product: nouns become 34px outline pills with 1px border and a tinted hue inside a 20px sentence, line step about 44px, with one consistent pill style. The sentence replaces a feature list.

Long reading at 16-20px, line-height 1.5-1.65, 576-690px measure (about 70 characters), paragraph gap 20-30px. On dark use about 82% ink, near 13:1, and lift emphasis by weight and brightness. Links keep a 1px underline offset 3px. Subheads 20-24px with 48px above and 16px below.

Paragraph in muted ink, 16-21px, with proper nouns or key phrases lifted to full ink, with an optional +100 weight. Size never changes. Skimming only the dark words must give the argument. Two to five lifts per paragraph. A single accent or 1px underline is an acceptable alternative.

One paragraph, no separate title: a short bold phrase ending in a full stop, then regular text in the same ink on the same line. 16-18px, line-height 1.3-1.55, about 460px measure, 16-24px under the image. Or keep one weight and use two inks. Never both.

One size carries the whole page, anywhere from 12 to 35px, one weight. Hierarchy comes only from ink, position, case or italic: full ink for current, 50-60% for labels. Line-height 1.15-1.75. The grid does the structural work.

Serif carries all sentences at 15-21px, line-height 1.45-1.5; grotesque carries names, titles and labels at the same or a slightly smaller size. Measure 376-612px. No colour change needed, since family alone marks the role.

A short paragraph at 24-76px with display treatment: line-height 1.0-1.3, tracking to -0.03em, weight 300-400, 620-1100px wide. Once per page. Grey on dark at 24/33 stays quiet; serif italic at 45/45 becomes a voice.

Body or notes in mono or duospace, 12-16px, line-height 1.25-1.65, slightly open fit of +0.02em at 14-16px, measure under 690px. Use duospace for long text and true mono only for short notes and captions.

Within 17-46px prose, one clause per passage gets a physical mark: rough pale marker strokes per line overshooting about 10px, a rounded 3px outline around a word, inline pictograms, or an inline italic serif in a sans paragraph. The mark replaces bold.

Legal as typesetting: 12-15px, muted but readable, numbered notes with numerals hanging in the gutter, on the grid, tied to superscripts above, closed with a 1px rule. Alternatively three calm centred lines at 15/28, or two clamped lines with a fade and a Read more link.

Copy set as rows: label column and answer column on one baseline, 15/24, answers about 515px wide, 24px between groups. Or feature rows with a 14px check, about 30px pitch, wrapped lines hanging under the label, a 1px dotted underline marking a tooltip.

A narrow caption column 250-480px wide, 11-17px, line-height 1.25-1.55, beside large imagery or a title and set apart from the main flow. A scale jump of about 1:10 makes it read as a note. Keep it off busy images.

Pull quotes at about 18px, line-height 1.4-1.6, muted ink, with the opening quotation mark hung about 7px outside the column so the first letter aligns with the text above. Use a pseudo-element, since Chrome ignores hanging-punctuation.

Price 36-64px in the display sans, weight 500-700, tracking -0.02 to -0.05em; unit 14-16px on the same baseline in grey or mono, 4-10px gap. The word Custom takes the same size so columns align. Reserve a fixed line above for billing notes so all prices sit level.

Price at body size: 13-15px weight 600 rate, regular unit, grey add-on lines prefixed with a plus, in a stack about 90px tall. No oversized number; the plan name carries the weight. Hierarchy comes from weight and ink only.

One stat at 100-150px beside a quote, or up to three at 48-72px, weight 400-700, tracking -0.02 to -0.04em, proportional figures, caption 14-30px 4-12px below. Set units at half size in a lighter ink. Long counters take slight positive tracking. Accent at most one figure.

Stats as ledger rows: numeral 48-64px at left, 14px mono caps caption on the same baseline at right or below, 1px rule between rows. Serif numerals feel especially right. Reads as entries, not hero numbers.
Mono values at about 18px in ruled grid cells with 10px uppercase mono labels beneath in mid-grey, tabular figures. Values may count up on entry.

Oldstyle figures in running dates or in stats near 55px, so digits drop below the baseline and numbers feel literary. Confirm the face has them and set oldstyle-nums. Spell out months and use en dashes. Never in a table.

Digits roll vertically in a mask of one line height, stopping one by one, tabular-nums, at 14-140px. Trigger on entry, or tie to scroll or load. Render the real final value in the HTML so it survives no script and reduced motion.

Numerals as structure: a current index at 90-180px with a small denominator near 50px on the same baseline, a year pinned 35px from a bottom corner, or a 12px two-digit index before each row. They give the page a sense of place.

One rate on a plaque: a roughly 154px serif numeral with the percent and unit stacked beside it, on a light plaque inside a 20px-radius tile, with an illustration breaking the tile edge. One per page.

Close the page with the wordmark at 90-100% of container width, flush to the margins, weight 600-700, tracking -0.03 to -0.05em, cropped by the viewport bottom by 10-25% of cap height. Fit by measuring, not by guessing vw. One tone, mask or lit detail may be added.

Brand name fills the first screen edge to edge, 16-32px side margins, 130-300px tall, under or behind the nav. Let renders overlap it, or set it tone on tone near 1.1:1 as a watermark. The headline sits below at about a quarter of the size. Nav omits the logo.

A short line scaled to fill the container: 135-318px, line-height 0.75-0.85, tracking -0.04 to -0.05em, alone in a plain viewport, or two lines force-justified to the margins. Once per page, as a section break or sign-off. Fit the size by measuring.

Giant name at 250-360px behind a cut-out object or centred image that overlaps about a third of the letters. Letters run off an edge. Text stays flat while the object carries the shadow. The name must stay readable from what remains.

Headline at 45-80px with real objects in the line: photo chips, clock tiles, product cards, pills, about 1em tall, each a different shape, holding real content, radius 10-14px, 1px border, at most two per line. Raise line-height to 1.15-1.25 to clear them. The words alone must still be a sentence.

Letters as windows: clip a photo, gradient or live canvas through heavy condensed type at 200px or more with background-clip. A flat full stop keeps the word anchored. Keep the image simple enough that word shapes survive.
A chapter opener with a single year, word or set of initials at 300-920px wide, alone on a plain ground with only the nav remaining. Use between long sections. It may recolour per chapter.

Lines resolve on scroll: upcoming text blurred 6-10px at 30% opacity, sharpening as it reaches reading position. A static form steps each line dimmer, at 100%, 80%, then 60% ink, like baked poster text. Provide a fully legible state under reduced motion.

Single nouns swap to a transparent fill with a 1px stroke at the same size, inside solid lines, at most one per sentence, at 64px or above. Or a wall of outlined names with the active one filled. Use a face with simple contours.
A list at 52-64px replaces a grid: centred terms split by 5px squares, or client names stacked, about 86px row pitch. Hover fills a 4px-radius block behind a term. Inline badges can carry live data.
Letters built from something else: voxels, wind strands, a pixel grid, brush. Treat as artwork at section-break scale, one per site, with a live text alternative for readers and search.
Hand-drawn strokes on type: uneven ovals around a figure, pencil arrows into text, scrawled circles around names. Use SVG paths, drawn on entry. Annotation replaces section dividers.

Text lines each wrapped in a flat bright strip with 2px side padding, black text, bottom-left of a full-bleed slide. Use box-decoration-break: clone so padding repeats per line. It guarantees contrast over any photograph.

Typography as concept: the product name as a dictionary entry with phonetics and a small tag, or a forced-break monologue of caps at 40/44 in a 520px column. One idea, set exactly. The content must earn it.
